'''David Ricardo Johnson''' (born February 26, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Tasmania JackJumpers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]], and was drafted by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]].

==Early life==
Johnson grew up in [[Louisville, Kentucky]], and attended [[Trinity High School (Louisville)|Trinity High School]]. As a sophomore, Johnson averaged 10.5 points and 4.8 rebounds per game and was named third team All-State.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kareell|first=David|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2017/05/25/trinitys-david-johnson-called-into-usa-basketball-under-16-training-camp/346084001/|title=Trinity's David Johnson called into USA Basketball Under-16 training camp|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=May 25, 2017|accessdate=March 17, 2020}}</ref> He was named first team All-State as a junior after averaging 13.9 points, 5.8 rebounds and 5.2 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2018/04/13/kentucky-boys-basketball-all-state-trinitys-david-johnson/513514002/|title=Kentucky boys basketball All-State: Trinity's David Johnson|first=Jason|last=Frakes|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=April 13, 2018|access-date=March 17, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/kentucky/2018/11/16/stronger-david-johnson-looking-lead-trinity-and-mr-basketball-race/1977487002/|title=Stronger David Johnson looking to lead Trinity and Mr Basketball race|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=November 16, 2018|access-date=March 17, 2020}}</ref> Johnson was ranked a four-star recruit and the best college prospect in the state of Kentucky by [[ESPN]] and committed to play at Louisville early during his senior year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Four-star-guard-David-Johnson-commits-to-Louisville-122293724/|title=Four-star guard David Johnson commits to Louisville|first=Evan|last=Daniels|website=247Sports.com|date=September 22, 2018|access-date=March 17, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1025842/2019/06/19/a-look-at-louisville-bound-guard-david-johnson/|title=A look at Louisville-bound guard David Johnson|first=Jeff|last=Greer|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=June 19, 2019|access-date=March 17, 2020}}</ref> He de-committed after Louisville was named as part of the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]], but recommitted after considering offers from Georgia and Xavier.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/trinity-basketball-star-david-johnson-commits-to-hometown-louisville-again|title=Trinity basketball star David Johnson commits to hometown Louisville — again|first=Danielle|last=Lerner|website=USATodayHSS.com|date=September 23, 2018|access-date=March 17, 2020}}</ref> As a senior, Johnson averaged 16.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and four assists per game and was named First Team All-State and the Player of the Year by the ''[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]''. He was named the MVP of the Kentucky Sweet 16 state tournament after recording 22 points, 12 rebounds, two assists and four blocked shots in the state title game.<ref name=crawford>{{cite web|url=https://www.wdrb.com/sports/louisville-freshman-david-johnson-injures-shoulder-could-be-out-/article_2c14972e-aef1-11e9-8152-7b0f024e5518.html|title=Louisville freshman David Johnson injures shoulder, could be out 4-6 months|first=Eric|last=Crawford|website=WDRB.com|date=July 25, 2019|access-date=March 17, 2020}}</ref> He scored 1,472 points and grabbed 719 rebounds in four seasons as a starter at Trinity.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/louisville/Article/louisville-mens-basketball-david-johnson-chris-mack-trinity-high-school-georgia-tech-142476365/|title=Louisville freshman David Johnson not expected to miss any time|first=Jody|last=Demling|website=247Sports.com|date=January 20, 2020|access-date=March 17, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
Johnson missed the beginning of his freshman season with an offseason shoulder injury.<ref name=crawford/><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/ulmbb-johnson-progressions|title=David Johnson continues to progress for Louisville backcourt|first=Sam|last=Draut|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]|date=January 17, 2020|accessdate=March 17, 2020}}</ref> Johnson played mostly as a key reserve during his freshman season with occasional starts. He scored a season high 19 points with seven assists, four rebounds and three steals in Louisville's upset win over [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] on January 18, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/01/18/david-johnson-shines-as-no-11-louisville-beats-no-3-duke-79-73/|title=David Johnson shines as No. 11 Louisville beats No. 3 Duke, 79-73|first=Rob|last=Dauster|website=[[NBC Sports]]|date=January 18, 2020|accessdate=March 17, 2020}}</ref> Johnson started at point guard against [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] on February 19, 2020, and led the team with seven assists in the 90–66 win in addition to three points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wdrb.com/sports/bozich-for-starters-david-johnson-leads-louisville-past-syracuse/article_aae2fa40-539d-11ea-b62d-8fc02a921540.html|title=For starters, David Johnson leads Louisville past Syracuse|first=Rich|last=Bozich|website=WDRB.com|date=February 19, 2020|accessdate=March 17, 2020}}</ref> Johnson averaged 6.3 points, 2.8 assists and 2.8 rebounds per game in 27 games with four starts for the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2020/03/10/louisville-basketball-david-johnson-could-key-postseason-run/4824527002/|title=Louisville basketball: David Johnson could be key to postseason run|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=March 10, 2020|accessdate=March 17, 2020}}</ref> As a sophomore, he averaged 12.6 points, 3.2 assists and 5.8 rebounds per game. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bozich |first1=Rick |title=David Johnson leaving Louisville basketball for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.wdrb.com/sports/david-johnson-leaving-louisville-basketball-for-2021-nba-draft/article_c8ed4cbc-9d38-11eb-b36a-9bc29881a814.html |access-date=June 24, 2021 |work=WDRB |date=April 14, 2021}}</ref> where he was a projected lottery pick.<ref>{{Cite web|last=McGavic|first=Matthew|title=Raptors select David Johnson in Second Round of 2021 NBA Draft|url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/david-johnson-drafted|access-date=2021-08-08|website=Sports Illustrated|language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Toronto Raptors and Raptors 905 (2021–2023)===
Johnson was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 47th pick by the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Shannon|last=Russell|title=Louisville guard David Johnson taken by Toronto Raptors in NBA draft's second round|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2021/07/30/nba-draft-david-johnson-taken-second-round-toronto-raptors/8089346002/|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=July 30, 2021|access-date=August 2, 2021}}</ref> On August 8, 2021, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with Toronto, splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, [[Raptors 905]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Toronto Raptors|title=Dreams into reality. We've signed @davidjohnson13 to a two-way contract. #WeTheNorth|number=1424718964379185158|user=Raptors|date=August 9, 2021|access-date=August 14, 2021}}</ref> That month, he played for Toronto during the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].<ref name=realgm>{{cite web |title=David Johnson Player Profile, Memphis Grizzlies - RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/David-Johnson/Summary/132437 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=27 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He played two NBA games for Toronto during the [[2021–22 Toronto Raptors season|2021–22 season]],<ref>{{cite web |title=David Johnson Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/johnsda08.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=27 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref> as well as 34 games in the G League for Raptors 905.<ref>{{cite web |title=David Johnson G-League Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/j/johnsda08d.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=27 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

After playing for Toronto in the [[2022 NBA Summer League]],<ref name="realgm" /> Johnson signed an [[Exhibit 10]] contract on October 15, 2022, but was waived later that day.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Aaron|last=Rose|title=Raptors Sign David Johnson, Reggie Perry, and Others to Exhibit 10 Deals|url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/news/toronto-raptors-sign-david-johnson-reggie-perry-to-exhibit-10-contracts|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=October 15, 2022|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref> He then re-joined Raptors 905 for the [[2022–23 NBA G League season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=David Johnson: Joins G League's 905|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/david-johnson-joins-g-leagues-905/|website=CBSSports.com|date=October 26, 2022|access-date=February 1, 2023}}</ref>

Johnson played for the Toronto Raptors in the [[2023 NBA Summer League]].<ref name="realgm" />

===Memphis Hustle (2023–2025)===
On October 18, 2023, Johnson signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Adonis Arms and David Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-adonis-arms-and-david-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}}</ref> However, he was waived three days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies finalize 2023/24 Opening Night roster|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-finalize-2023-24-opening-night-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}}</ref> He subsequently joined the [[Memphis Hustle]] for the [[2023–24 NBA G League season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2023-24 training camp roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2023-24-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=November 7, 2023}}</ref>

On October 16, 2024, Johnson signed once again with the Grizzlies,<ref>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign David Johnson|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-david-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2024|access-date=October 17, 2024}}</ref> but was waived the same day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Miles Norris|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-miles-norris|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2024|access-date=October 17, 2024}}</ref> He subsequently re-joined the Memphis Hustle for the [[2024–25 NBA G League season]].<ref name="realgm" />

===Tasmania JackJumpers (2025–present)===
On May 27, 2025, Johnson signed with the [[Tasmania JackJumpers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the [[2025–26 NBL season|2025–26 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=JackJumpers sign dynamic import |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/jackjumpers-sign-dynamic-import |access-date=27 May 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=27 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref> On September 26, 2025, he was ruled out for four weeks after suffering a calf injury at practice.<ref>{{cite news |title=Star JackJumper sidelined |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/star-jackjumper-david-johnson-sidelined |access-date=26 September 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=26 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He missed an additional month after re-aggravating the injury during rehabilitation.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tassie gets a Johnson Jump-start |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/timely-return-for-jackjumpers-star-david-johnson |access-date=20 November 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=20 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref> On February 1, 2026, he had a game-high 33 points and seven 3-pointers in a 91–89 win over the [[New Zealand Breakers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=DJ shoots JackJumpers to pivotal win |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/dj-shoots-jackjumpers-to-pivotal-win |access-date=1 February 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=1 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

On June 5, 2026, Johnson re-signed with the JackJumpers for the [[2026–27 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=JackJumpers re-sign sharpshooting import |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/tasmania-jackjumpers-re-sign-sharpshooting-import-david-johnson |access-date=5 June 2026 |work=nbl.com.au |date=5 June 2026 |language=en}}</ref>
